hints: Look closely at the two different double bonds in the structure, one C=C and one C=O, and recall what each double bond contributes.
Count the pi bonds first, then focus only on the two oxygen atoms to work out the total lone pairs.
Think about the shape around the CH3 carbons and whether tetrahedral single-bonded groups can ever be flat with the rest of the molecule.
walkthrough:
**Draw out the full structure**

Let's expand the formula so we can see every bond. Tiglic acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{C}(=\text{O})\text{OH}$.

So we have an alkene $\text{C}=\text{C}$ joined to a carboxylic acid $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ plus two methyl groups.

**Check statement 1, count pi bonds**

Remember, every double bond contains one sigma bond and one pi bond.

$$\text{number of } \pi \text{ bonds} = 1 \text{ (from C=C)} + 1 \text{ (from C=O)} = 2$$
So statement 1 is correct.

**Check statement 2, count lone pairs**

Only oxygen has lone pairs here. Carbon and hydrogen have none in this neutral molecule.

In $-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$: $\text{C}=\text{O}$ oxygen has 2 lone pairs, $\text{C}-\text{O}-\text{H}$ oxygen has 2 lone pairs.

$$2 + 2 = 4 \text{ lone pairs}$$
So statement 2 is correct.

**Check statement 3, test for planarity**

The $\text{C}=\text{C}$ and $\text{C}=\text{O}$ parts are planar, but the two $\text{CH}_3$ groups are tetrahedral $sp^3$ carbons.

Tetrahedral means the three H atoms point above and below the plane, so they cannot all lie in the same plane. So statement 3 is incorrect.

Conclusion: 1 and 2 only are correct.

options.A: This claims 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statements 1 and 2 are right, but 3 is wrong because the methyl $\text{CH}_3$ carbons are tetrahedral, so their hydrogens stick out of the plane.
options.B: This claims 1 and 2 only are correct. This is right: there are two pi bonds (one in C=C, one in C=O) and four lone pairs (two on each oxygen), but the molecule is not fully planar due to the $sp^3$ methyl groups.
options.C: This claims 2 and 3 only are correct. It wrongly leaves out statement 1, which is definitely true, and wrongly includes statement 3, which fails because of tetrahedral $\text{CH}_3$ hydrogens.
options.D: This claims 1 only is correct. It correctly includes 1 but wrongly rejects 2. The carboxylic acid group clearly has four lone pairs in total on its two oxygens.
